messages:
Maya: quick sync — we need a concrete governance proposal for reserved pools + graceful degradation before next week. customers pushing for clearer SLAs and runbook.
Jordan: agreed. what's the primary risk we need to mitigate? cost overcommit or noisy tenants?
Maya: both, but customer asks are mostly about predictable latency during surges. they want a contract that guarantees tail latency under committed throughput and defined behavior when bursts exceed commit.
Priya: idea: define 3 states for a pool: steady (<= commit), burst (commit < usage <= commit + burst_credit), and degraded (> commit + burst_credit). each state has explicit routing and eviction rules.
Anil: for degraded, do we want automatic fallback to smaller model or queue requests? fallback impacts quality, queuing impacts latency. need product decision.
Morgan: ops perspective — queuing is simpler to reason about for SLOs: we can expose a max-queue-ms and circuit-break after threshold. fallback requires model compatibility and evals per customer.
Jordan: can we combine? first try short tail queuing (e.g., 200ms window), then soft-fallback to quantized variant if queue exceeded and customer opted in.
Maya: that hybrid seems promising. customers could opt-in to fallback in their contract. for those who don't, we queue then 429 if queue full.
Priya: need metrics to qualify launch: 95th/99th token latency under synthetic surge, >=99.9% availability at commit level, documented behavior for burst drains, and billing clarity for burst units consumed.
Anil: add observability checklist: per-tenant burst burn rate, queue length histogram, fallback count and quality delta (user-reported + automated eval).
Morgan: ops runbook notes: escalation path when pool is degraded > 10min, steps to preempt low-priority tenants (policy-based), and how to manually increase burst credit for churny customers.
Maya: can we standardize preemption priority tiers? Tier A (SLA-paid) -> Tier B (committed) -> Tier C (best-effort). Preemption should only affect Tier C for first 5min of surge.
Jordan: sounds reasonable. need to map to billing: Tier A reserved customers shouldn't pay for bursts? or we bill bursts at premium rate?
Priya: prefer transparent pricing: committed usage billed at baseline, bursts billed at higher rate. Tier A can buy burst-included packages. document examples in the FAQ.
Anil: small technical ask: we need an eviction token bucket algorithm; proposal: per-tenant token bucket where tokens = commit + carried_over_burst, drain on token consumption, refill per minute. preemption chooses tenants with lowest SLA score first.
Morgan: ops-bot: schedule a staging test to validate bucket refill behavior for burst carryover.
ops-bot: scheduled: /job reserved-pools-burst-sim on staging, start: 2187655000, owners: @Morgan @Anil
Maya: next steps: (1) Priya draft the governance doc with states + metrics, (2) Anil produce eviction algorithm spec + pseudocode, (3) Morgan own runbook + staging test. deliverables due EOD Thu.
Priya: on it — I'll include sample contract language and billing examples.
Anil: will write pseudocode and perf constraints (O(n) preemption selection, target <200ms decision latency).
Morgan: I'll add runbook steps and tie the staging job to our alerting so we can test notifications.
Jordan: FYI I'll start a short customer comms draft clarifying behavior during degradation and opt-in fallback choices.
Maya: awesome. if no objections, we'll lock this approach and include as launch criteria for reserved pools GA. :thumbsup:
Priya: +1
Anil: +1
Morgan: +1
Jordan: +1
Maya: thanks — closing thread, will create PR for the doc after Priya's draft.
